publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Capturing the Action: Changes in Newsgathering Technology
abstract: The author presents a brief review of some of the historical landmarks in TV news broadcasting beginning with the early 1920s and continuing to the 1990s. The author goes on to consider the benefits which digital technology will bring.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Capturing the Action: Changes in Newsgathering Technology
abstract: The author discusses the use of technology and automation in video newsroom operations, drawing on his own experiences of working in television.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Capturing the Action: Changes in Newsgathering Technology
abstract: In covering the issues of the technology of newsgathering on location, this paper will deal with transmission, and to a degree, the acquisition of material for news bulletins, including 'live' material, from difficult locations around the world-specifically war-zones and remote areas. Most readers are assumed to be familiar with current ENG technology, but perhaps are not so conversant with the current state of SNG, so we will be examining this in conjunction with the logistics of deployment and the problems faced in maintaining both ENG and SNG equipment in the field. Finally, the question of the technology newsgatherers need to use in the future will be considered.

articleTitle: DVCPRO: Playing to the strengths of tape
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Capturing the Action: Changes in Newsgathering Technology
abstract: The television production and transmission world are in a state of flux. New developments challenge traditional thinking with almost monotonous regularity. Yet some things seem never to change; last years' programmes were better than this years and a new VTR format is about to be released are two of the given truths of the TV business. Even now, in the age of generally available hard disc video recording, the second holds true. This paper examines the case for a new VTR format in general and argues that to compete in a world where other solutions may be possible, tape based systems will need to specialise to succeed. The DVCPRO recording format is an example of this new approach, by focusing on ENG acquisition it can offer system advantages not possible with other technologies or general purpose systems.

articleTitle: The digital newsroom-technology war zone or peace talks?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Capturing the Action: Changes in Newsgathering Technology
abstract: Peace is in sight on the battlegrounds of digital technology for television. Users are understanding the benefits of the diverse approaches and with some further conversations at the image, interchange and control protocol levels, harmonious solutions will emerge. Nowhere more than the digital newsroom will these be put to the test. The benefits of success are clear, the alternative is the old story of killing the messenger!.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Capturing the Action: Changes in Newsgathering Technology
abstract: This paper identifies new technology which is helping to deliver a radically improved news making process. The strengths and weaknesses of today's practices are acknowledged and broadcasters' future requirements are analysed. As the shape of a new integrated IT based solution takes shape some of the technical issues which arise from this approach are considered.
